column1: # winprofile.ini escape vectors. The codecs are described in
# doc/winprofile-ini.md. Data rather than a callable function because no front
# end can call another's codec from its unit tests.
# raw spells those four bytes \r \n \t \\ and is otherwise literal ASCII.
# ASCII only: winprofile.ini declares no charset and the three front ends do not
# agree on one, so a non-ASCII vector passes in one place and mangles in another.
# state=agreed: all three encode raw to encoded and decode it back. Assert both
# state=divergent: they disagree, encoded is empty, the note says how.
# A consumer SKIPS these and COUNTS the skip, or the marker hides cases.

column4: a space is not escaped by any of the three
CR, the byte that would otherwise end the line
a CRLF pair encodes as two escapes
a lone dash is not a marker
WinHTTrack writes a%3db, the other two write it raw
WebHTTrack writes a%22b in its unquoted fields, the others raw
decode: WinHTTrack gives a space, the other two give A
decode: WinHTTrack is case-sensitive and gives a space
decode: WinHTTrack a space, WebHTTrack passes it, Android throws
decode: a truncated escape, Android throws where the others do not
